items.title: Deterministic workspace-root overflow has no selection or churn algorithm
items.statement: The cap and visibility requirement are explicit, but the authoritative core does not define root ordering, tie-breaking, stability when documents open or close, when an excluded root is promoted, or whether a root may be evicted while requests are in flight.
items.impact: At more than ten eligible roots, two conforming implementations can expose different workspaces and can churn server state differently during document activity.
items.builder_discretion: Do not choose ordering, eviction, promotion, or in-flight transition semantics as incidental implementation details.

items.title: Workspace-path logs and evidence lack a privacy lifecycle
items.statement: Overflow exclusions must be visible in logs and evidence, but the core supplies no path minimization or redaction rule, access boundary, retention duration, deletion behavior, or rule for exporting evidence that may reveal local workspace names and layout.
items.impact: Local paths or project identity can persist or be disclosed through support and audit artifacts beyond the purpose of overflow diagnosis.
items.builder_discretion: Do not infer that full paths are safe to retain or export merely because visibility is required.

items.title: Debounced refresh omits stale-response, cancellation, and server-loss transitions
items.statement: The refresh triggers and delays are named, but the core does not define document-version capture, cancellation and replacement of pending debounce work, response ordering after another edit, behavior during close or root eviction, retry after timeout, or rehydration after an LSP process exits and restarts.
items.impact: Late inlay-hint or hover responses can overwrite newer truth, and process or timeout failures can leave an open document permanently stale.
items.builder_discretion: Do not invent stale-response acceptance, retry, cancellation, or restart recovery semantics.

dimension_assessments.summary: Prerequisite and cross-document units have empty dependency and consumer edges despite phase and external-contract semantics.
Invalid persisted values and async document or server lifecycle transitions have no canonical state machine.
Debounced responses and multi-file writes lack version, cancellation, concurrent-change, and ordering semantics.
Timeout or server loss, mid-batch edit failure, and redb write failure lack defined partial-result behavior.
No restart rehydration, edit rollback, rollback-failure reporting, or persisted-config recovery policy is present.
The FileSafe mutation boundary is explicit, but server command and environment modification authority is not defined and payload protections remain externally unverified.
Workspace-path evidence and environment-bearing server configuration lack redaction, retention, deletion, and disclosure rules.
Command, env, initialization, and server-supplied edit payload validation is absent or only delegated without evidence in the authorized core.
GUI surfaces are named but truthful stale, loading, partial, blocked, and overflow states are not specified locally and external GUI owners were intentionally unread.
The core selects a stdio-capable client and defines no network transport; network loss is not applicable to this window, while local server-process loss is separately a recovery gap.
The ten-root cap is explicit, but selection churn is undefined and command, initialization, edit-set, log, and evidence sizes have no stated bounds.
Chat affordances and Problems links are GUI-related, but accessibility is neither specified locally nor verifiable without forbidden external owner reads.
No localizable copy, message taxonomy, text expansion, or locale behavior is present in this window; external GUI coverage is unknown.
Default-versus-config precedence and redb schema evolution, downgrade, corruption, and client-change compatibility are undefined.
Overflow visibility is explicitly required, but evidence privacy and behavioral oracles are absent, and no structured fields or recovery diagnostics are defined.
Approval and FileSafe routing are explicit non-gaps, but multi-file preflight, atomicity, concurrent-change detection, and rollback remain open.
Virtual-document and GUI behavior rely on external SSOT owners without dependency edges or locally verifiable closure.
The listed checks validate plan migration and index structure rather than the accepted runtime, safety, persistence, or GUI behaviors.

The blind window cannot establish the contents or change state of referenced FileSafe, Tools, FileManager, and FinalGUISpec owners, so delegated protections and presentation closure remain bounded unknowns.
